s05's TodoWrite lets an agent record the steps of its current task. Each checklist item has content and a status, helping the agent keep track of what remains.

`agent_loop`) and `reactive_compact` on prompt-too-long errors (at most once
per turn).

### Cron job

A scheduled prompt — a 5-field cron expression plus prompt, stored apart from
conversation history (`CronJob`, `schedule_job`, `validate_cron` in
`code.py`). A daemon scheduler thread (`cron_scheduler_loop`) ticks each
second and enqueues due jobs (deduped by a per-minute `_last_fired` marker);
`agent_loop` then consumes the queue as `[Scheduled]` user messages.
`durable` jobs persist to `.scheduled_tasks.json`, and one-shot jobs use
`pending_delivery` with `acknowledge_cron_jobs` / `restore_cron_jobs` for
at-least-once delivery.

`RecoveryState` + `with_retry` in `code.py` wrap every model call with up to

switch to `FALLBACK_MODEL_ID` if configured. Separately, `agent_loop` recovers

7. When: edges may be added only while the target task is still pending and unowned; the target and all dependencies must exist, and new edges may not introduce self-dependencies or cycles (repeated edges are safe/no-op) (s10 README, "update_task: Add Dependencies with Returned IDs"; s15 GLOSSARY, "Task board").

Q2 answer (teams work flow + plan gate):
1. Work — spawn-time assignment: Lead creates the Task first and passes its task_id to `spawn_teammate`, which "claims the initial Task before the thread starts"; a failed claim prevents the teammate from starting. (s13_agent_teams/README.md, "1. Lead proposes a team and waits for user confirmation" and "2. Every teammate owns an independent loop")
2. Work — idle auto-claim: an IDLE teammate first waits on its MessageBus mailbox (direct messages have priority), then scans the shared task board and auto-claims the next ready task via `claim_next_task`. (README.md, "6. IDLE checks the mailbox before looking for ready tasks"; s15_integrated_harness/GLOSSARY.md, "Teammate")
3. Claim is atomic: `claim_task` re-validates pending/unowned/unblocked status under `task_store_lock()`, so many teammates may discover the same candidate but only one claim moves it to `in_progress`; an owner must finish its current task before claiming another. (README.md, "7. Discovery and claim are separate, and claim is atomic")
4. Both entry points feed the same WORK loop with the same plan gate, result reporting, and shutdown protocol. (README.md, "8. Claimed work reuses the same WORK loop")
5. Separate events: `result` answers "What did this assignment produce?" while `idle_notification` answers "Can this teammate accept more work?"; one vague "done" cannot represent both facts. (README.md, "5. Result and IDLE are separate events")
6. Plan gate while unapproved (state `required`/`pending`/`rejected`): blocks `bash`, `write_file`, and `edit_file` — the teammate can still read files and submit or revise a plan. (README.md, "12. Plan approval constrains execution")
7. Additionally, the gate hard-blocks `complete_task` until the lead approves a submitted plan, and `advance_assignment_version` re-arms the gate to `required` on each new claim so old approvals never leak into new work. (GLOSSARY.md, "Plan gate")

Work — idle auto-claim: an IDLE teammate first waits on its MessageBus mailbox (direct messages have priority), then scans the shared task board and auto-claims the next ready task via `claim_next_task`. (README.md, "6. IDLE checks the mailbox before looking for ready tasks"; s15_integrated_harness/GLOSSARY.md, "Teammate")

Claim is atomic: `claim_task` re-validates pending/unowned/unblocked status under `task_store_lock()`, so many teammates may discover the same candidate but only one claim moves it to `in_progress`; an owner must finish its current task before claiming another. (README.md, "7. Discovery and claim are separate, and claim is atomic")

7. Additionally, the gate hard-blocks `complete_task` until the lead approves a submitted plan, and `advance_assignment_version` re-arms the gate to `required` on each new claim so old approvals never leak into new work. (GLOSSARY.md, "Plan gate")
